A Click-to-WhatsApp ad that opens a chat with her business
quiz.explain: Click-to-WhatsApp ads send interested people straight into a chat, which is where she sells.

quiz.q: In a Meta campaign, where do you choose the audience and budget?
quiz.explain: The campaign holds the objective; ad sets hold the audience, placements, budget and schedule; ads hold the creative.

quiz.q: Which audience is usually the warmest and most likely to respond?
options: People who engaged with your Instagram or watched your videos in the last 60 days
A random interest such as football
quiz.explain: A retargeting custom audience already knows you, so they respond more often.

quiz.q: Uche wants to know if a video ad beats a flyer ad. What is the best test?
options: Run them in different months to different audiences
Run both to the same audience at the same time with equal budgets
Run only the one he likes
Change the audience, copy and image all at once
quiz.explain: Keeping everything the same except the creative shows which creative really performs better.

quiz.q: Rukayat spends 14,000 naira and gets 10 orders. Her profit per order before ads is 2,500 naira. What is her cost per order, and is the ad profitable?
quiz.explain: 14,000 ÷ 10 = 1,400 naira per order, which is below her 2,500 naira profit, so each order still earns about 1,100 naira.

quiz.q: Three days after launch, an ad set is in the learning phase and results look uneven. What should she do?
options: Let it run, and judge results over about a week unless costs are clearly unaffordable
Edit the audience and creative every morning
quiz.explain: Frequent edits restart learning. Give it time, while keeping an eye on spend.

modules.title: Analytics, Growth and Strategy
modules.overview: Measure what your social media is really doing for your business, work with micro-influencers and partners, sell directly through catalogues and safe payment links, and bring everything together into a 90-day plan you can review and improve.

lessons.title: Reading your Insights and measuring real results
objectives: Define reach, views, engagement, engagement rate, clicks and conversions
Find Insights in Meta Business Suite, Instagram and TikTok
Calculate engagement rate for a post
Build a simple monthly tracking sheet that links posts to sales

blocks.text: **Analytics** (called Insights on Meta and Analytics on TikTok) are the numbers the platforms give you about your account and posts. They tell you who saw your content, what they did, and which posts brought people closer to buying. Without them you are guessing. With them you can do more of what works and stop what does not.
The key words

head: Metric
What it means
What it tells you
rows: Number of different accounts that saw your content
Number of times content was shown or played, including repeats
How often it was seen; Meta now reports views in many places
How strongly the people who saw it reacted
People who went to your profile or tapped your link

blocks.name: social-dashboard
blocks.alt: A dashboard of social media charts and numbers
blocks.caption: Insights show what happened; your tracking sheet connects it to enquiries and sales.

blocks.text: Where to find your numbers

items: **Meta Business Suite:** Insights section for Facebook and Instagram together, with results, audience age, gender and top cities, and content performance.
**Instagram app:** tap Professional dashboard on your profile, or View insights under any post or Reel.
**TikTok:** Business Suite or Analytics in the profile menu, with overview, content and followers tabs, including average watch time for each video.
**WhatsApp Business:** basic message statistics in the tools section, plus your own labels for orders.

blocks.title: From vanity to value
items: Sales and repeat customers
Messages and link clicks
Saves, shares, comments
Reach and views
blocks.caption: Reach is the base, but the numbers near the top are the ones that pay the bills.

blocks.title: Worked example: a monthly review
blocks.context: For example, Zainab sells handmade beaded jewellery in Kano through Instagram and WhatsApp. At the end of the month she reviews her 12 posts.
steps: Her best Reel reached 3,200 accounts and got 96 likes, 14 comments, 22 shares and 28 saves: 160 engagements.
Engagement rate = 160 ÷ 3,200 × 100 = 5 percent.
A product photo reached only 600 accounts but brought 11 WhatsApp chats, because the caption had a price and a clear call to action.
In her tracking sheet she counts 34 WhatsApp enquiries that mentioned Instagram and 13 orders from them.
Her decision: keep Reels for reach, but always add a price and call to action, and repeat the product-photo style twice a month.
blocks.result: Zainab now judges posts by what they do for sales, not only by likes, and her next month's plan is based on evidence.

blocks.text: Keep a simple tracking sheet

Platforms cannot see sales that happen in WhatsApp or by bank transfer, so keep your own sheet in a notebook, Excel or Google Sheets. Columns: date, platform, post, reach, engagements, enquiries, orders, revenue. Ask every buyer where they found you. Review once a month, at the same time, and write three decisions.
Understanding your audience data

Insights also tell you **who** your followers are: top cities, age ranges, gender and the times they are most active. Compare this with your customer sentence from Lesson 1.1. If you deliver in Abuja but most followers are in Lagos, your content or hashtags may be attracting the wrong people, or you may have a chance to offer nationwide delivery. If your buyers are mostly 30 to 45 but your followers are mostly 18 to 24, adjust your content style, topics and partners.

Use the "most active times" chart as a starting point for when to post, then test two or three time slots for a few weeks and keep the one that gives the best results. Look too at which posts brought **new followers**, because those topics are the ones introducing you to fresh people.

Finally, check the trend, not just the total. Is reach growing month by month? Are more enquiries coming from social media than three months ago? A steady upward trend matters more than one viral post.

items: **Weekly (10 minutes):** check messages answered, enquiries and orders in your sheet.
**Monthly (1 hour):** review Insights, ad results and the sheet together, then write three decisions.
**Quarterly:** compare the three months with your goals and update your plan (Lesson 4.4).

blocks.text: Screenshots help too. Save a screenshot of your account overview on the first day of each month, so you can compare months even if the app changes how it displays data.

blocks.title: Compare like with like
blocks.text: Compare Reels with Reels and carousels with carousels, over the same number of days after posting. A post that is one day old cannot fairly be compared with one that is two weeks old.

blocks.title: Small numbers are normal
blocks.text: When your account is small, numbers jump around. Look at patterns over several weeks rather than reacting to one post.

takeaways: Reach shows how far a post went; engagement shows whether people cared
Engagement rate = engagements ÷ reach × 100
Messages, orders and repeat customers matter more than likes
Keep your own sheet to connect posts to WhatsApp and transfer sales
Review monthly and write three decisions

activity.title: Your first monthly report
steps: Open Insights for the last 30 days on your main platform.
List each post with reach, engagements, saves and shares.
Calculate the engagement rate for your three best and three weakest posts.
Count enquiries and orders that came from social media this month.
Write three decisions for next month.
activity.evidence: Your tracking sheet for the month with engagement rates and three written decisions.

lessons.title: Working with micro-influencers and partner businesses
objectives: Explain the difference between micro-influencers and large influencers
Check an influencer's real engagement and audience fit before paying
Agree a simple written brief with deliverables and payment terms
Use paid partnership labels and collaboration features correctly

blocks.text: **Influencer marketing** means working with people who have an engaged audience so they show your product to their followers. **Collaborative marketing** is the same idea with other businesses: you share each other's audiences. For small businesses, the best partners are rarely celebrities. They are people and businesses your exact customers already trust.
Bigger is not always better

head: Type
Typical follower range (rough guide)
Strengths
Watch out for
rows: Close, trusting audience; often accept products or small fees
Good balance of reach and trust; often niche and local
High cost, broad audience, fake followers more common

blocks.name: influencer
blocks.alt: An influencer posting content to followers
blocks.caption: The right partner has an audience that matches your customer, not just a big follower count.

blocks.text: How to check an influencer before paying

items: **Audience fit:** do their followers live where you sell and look like your customer? Ask for a screenshot of their audience Insights (top cities, age, gender).
**Engagement:** look at their last 10 posts. Are comments real sentences from real people, or just emojis and "nice"?
**Average views:** for Reels or TikTok, note typical views, not their single most viral video.
**Past brand posts:** do sponsored posts still get real comments? Do they disclose partnerships?
**Results:** ask what results past clients got, and ask for a short reference if possible.

blocks.title: Choosing partners
items: Good fit, low engagement: test small
Good fit, high engagement: best choice
Poor fit, low engagement: avoid
Poor fit, high engagement: not for you
blocks.caption: Audience fit matters as much as engagement; a hugely engaged audience in the wrong city does not buy from you.

blocks.text: The brief and the agreement

Write down what you agreed, even for a small deal: deliverables (for example one Reel and three Stories), dates, key messages, what must not be said (such as health claims), whether you can reuse the content in ads, payment amount and timing, and how results will be tracked. A simple tracking method is a special discount code or a phrase like "Tell us Tolu sent you" so you can count orders.

blocks.title: Worked example: a micro-influencer deal
blocks.context: For example, Ifeoma runs a small bakery in Owerri. A local food reviewer with about 15,000 followers, mostly in Imo State, offers a Reel and Stories for 40,000 naira (approximate).
steps: Ifeoma checks the last 10 Reels: typical views are 8,000 to 12,000 with real comments asking where to buy.
She asks for audience Insights; most followers are in Owerri and aged 22 to 40.
They agree in writing: one Reel and three Stories, the bakery tagged with the Paid partnership label, code "OWERRI10" for 10 percent off, half paid before posting and half after.
Over two weeks, 22 orders use the code, averaging 9,000 naira (approximate) each, about 198,000 naira in sales.
With permission, Ifeoma reuses the Reel as an ad to her retargeting audience.
blocks.result: A carefully checked local partner brought trackable sales and a ready-made ad. The figures are illustrative.

blocks.text: Paying and measuring fairly

Common ways to pay creators are a fixed fee per post, free products in exchange for honest content (often called gifting), a commission on each sale through their code, or a mix such as a small fee plus commission. For a first test, a mix reduces your risk and rewards the creator for real results. Agree the payment method and dates in writing and pay on time; creators talk to each other, and a good reputation brings better partners.

Measure every partnership the same way: how many people used the code or mentioned the partner, how many orders and how much revenue came in, and what you paid. Divide total cost by orders to get your cost per order, exactly as you did for ads in Lesson 3.4. Compare partners with each other and with ads, and keep working with those who bring customers at a cost you can afford. Long-term relationships with a few reliable creators usually work better than one-off posts with many.

Start small. Test one creator with a modest deal before signing a longer agreement, and agree in advance what happens if the content is late, off-message or never posted. A clear, friendly brief protects both of you and makes the next collaboration easier. Keep copies of the final posts and your written agreement in one folder for future reference.

blocks.title: Disclose paid partnerships
blocks.text: Instagram, Facebook and TikTok require paid content to be disclosed, using tools such as Instagram's Paid partnership label or TikTok's content disclosure setting. Honest disclosure also protects trust in both of you.

blocks.title: Partner with businesses too
blocks.text: A bridal makeup artist, a gele tier and a photographer serve the same bride. Cross-promote, run a joint giveaway, or post Collab posts that appear on both accounts.

takeaways: Micro and nano influencers with the right local audience often give better value
Check audience fit, real comments and average views before paying
Put deliverables, payment and usage rights in writing
Track results with codes or referral phrases
Always disclose paid partnerships

activity.title: Shortlist three partners
steps: Find three influencers or businesses whose followers match your customer.
For each, review the last 10 posts and note average views and comment quality.
Place each one on the partner matrix.
Draft a one-page brief for your top choice with deliverables, dates, payment and tracking code.
activity.evidence: Your shortlist with notes, the matrix placement, and the draft brief.

lessons.title: Selling directly: catalogues, payments and delivery
objectives: Set up a WhatsApp Business catalogue and share product links
Choose safe payment options such as bank transfer, POS, payment links and pay on delivery
Write a clear ordering, delivery and returns policy
Protect yourself and customers from common online selling scams

blocks.text: **Social commerce** means selling directly through social media and messaging, without the customer needing to visit a shop or a separate website. In Nigeria much of this already happens through WhatsApp chats and bank transfers. Doing it well means making ordering clear, payment safe and delivery reliable, so happy customers come back and tell others.
Your selling toolkit

head: Tool
What it does
How to use it
rows: Shows products with photos, prices and descriptions inside WhatsApp
Share the catalogue or a single product link in chats and Status
Lists items for local buyers to browse
Good for items people search for locally
Customer pays by card, transfer or USSD through a link
Send the link in chat; you get a record of each payment
Bank transfer and POS (for example Moniepoint or Opay)
Direct payment to your business account
Use a business account name that matches your brand
Customer pays when the item arrives
Useful for trust with first-time buyers in your city; plan for failed deliveries

blocks.name: online-shopping
blocks.alt: A person shopping online on a phone
blocks.caption: Clear products, safe payment and reliable delivery turn social media attention into repeat customers.

blocks.text: A smooth ordering process

blocks.title: Order flow
items: Customer sees post
Chats on WhatsApp
Gets catalogue and total
Pays, payment confirmed
Packed and delivered
Asked for review
blocks.caption: Each step should be quick and clear, with no guessing about price, delivery fee or timing.

items: Send the product link or photo, price and delivery fee in one message.
Confirm size, colour and address in writing.
Send payment details or a payment link, and confirm payment in your own bank or payment app.
Send an order summary: items, total paid, delivery date.
Share the rider's name and expected arrival time.
After delivery, ask for a review and a photo, and invite them to save your number.

blocks.title: Worked example: a simple order policy
blocks.context: For example, Patience sells children's clothes in Benin City through Facebook and WhatsApp. She keeps getting the same questions about delivery and exchanges.
steps: She writes a short policy: "Orders confirmed after payment. Benin City delivery 1,500 naira (approximate), 1 to 2 days. Other states by park or courier, 2 to 5 days, fee depends on location. Exchanges for wrong size within 3 days if unworn with tags."
She saves it as a WhatsApp quick reply and pins it in a Facebook post and an Instagram Highlight.
She adds all products to the WhatsApp catalogue with sizes and prices.
She switches from personal account transfers to a business account named after her shop.
She sends a short order summary after every payment.
blocks.result: Fewer repeated questions, fewer disputes about exchanges, and more trust because customers pay to an account in her business name.

blocks.text: Turning one sale into many
Getting a new customer through social media costs time and often money. Selling again to someone who already trusts you is much cheaper, so plan for repeat orders from the start.

items: **Label buyers in WhatsApp Business** so you can find past customers when new stock arrives.
**Send a thank-you message** after delivery with a care tip, for example how to wash an Ankara dress so the colours last.
**Ask for a review** a few days later, and reshare it with permission.
**Offer a reason to come back,** such as early access to new stock for past buyers, or a small discount on a second order.

**Use broadcast lists carefully.** WhatsApp Business broadcast messages only reach people who have saved your number, and too many promotional messages can lead to blocks. Send useful updates, not daily adverts.

blocks.text: Packaging also sells. A neat package with a thank-you card and your handle printed on it encourages customers to post a photo and tag you, which brings in their friends.

Delivery is part of your marketing. Late or damaged deliveries lead to public complaints, while reliable delivery earns reviews. Compare two or three local dispatch riders or courier services, agree prices for each area in advance, and include the delivery fee in your quick reply so customers see the full total before paying. For interstate orders, give realistic timeframes and share the waybill or tracking details as soon as the parcel leaves.

blocks.title: Common scams to watch for
blocks.text: Fake bank alerts by SMS, edited payment screenshots, "overpayment" requests asking you to refund the difference, and buyers asking you to click links to "receive payment". Confirm every payment in your own bank or payment app before releasing goods, and never share your PIN, OTP or login details.

blocks.title: Register and price properly
blocks.text: Registering your business name with the Corporate Affairs Commission (CAC) lets you open a business bank account in that name, which builds trust. Check whether your product needs NAFDAC or SON approval before advertising it widely.

takeaways: Most Nigerian social selling closes in WhatsApp, so make that process smooth
Use a catalogue, clear prices and a delivery fee in the first reply
Offer safe payment options and confirm payment in your own app
Write and pin a short ordering, delivery and exchange policy
Know the common payment scams and never share PINs or OTPs

activity.title: Set up your shop in chat
steps: Add at least ten products to your WhatsApp Business catalogue with prices.
Write your ordering, delivery and exchange policy in under 80 words.
Save it as a quick reply and pin it on your main platform.
Create an order summary template.
Walk through one test order with a friend from enquiry to delivery and note anything confusing.
activity.evidence: Catalogue screenshot, your written policy, order summary template and notes from the test order.

lessons.title: Building your 90-day social media plan
objectives: Set SMART goals for social media linked to business results
Combine platforms, content pillars, ads and partnerships into one plan
Plan time and money for 90 days
Review results monthly and adjust the plan

blocks.text: A strategy is a plan for using limited time and money to reach a clear business goal. Many small businesses post every day without one, then feel tired and disappointed. A simple 90-day plan, reviewed each month, keeps you focused and shows what is really working.
Set SMART goals

A **SMART** goal is Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant and Time-bound. "Grow my page" is not SMART. "Get 60 WhatsApp enquiries and 20 orders from Instagram between January and March" is. Link at least one goal to sales, and one to building your audience.

blocks.name: social-strategy
blocks.alt: A person planning a social media strategy on a board
blocks.caption: A 90-day plan turns all the lessons in this course into one routine you can keep.

blocks.text: The parts of your plan

head: Part
What to decide
Course lesson
rows: Main, support and WhatsApp for sales
Pillars, formats, posting days, batching day
Monthly ad budget, objective, audiences, break-even
One partnership, catalogue, payment and delivery
Tracking sheet and monthly review date

blocks.title: The monthly improvement cycle
items: Plan the month
Create and post
Engage and sell
Measure results
Decide and adjust
blocks.caption: Every month you plan, act, measure and adjust, so the next month is better than the last.

blocks.title: Worked example: a 90-day plan for a tailoring business
blocks.context: For example, Hauwa runs a tailoring shop in Jos. She has about 5 hours a week for marketing and about 30,000 naira (approximate) a month for ads.
steps: Goal: 90 WhatsApp enquiries and 30 orders from social media in 90 days, and 1,000 new followers on Instagram.
Platforms: Instagram main, Facebook support, WhatsApp Business for orders.
Content: three posts a week (one Teach, one Show the work Reel, one Proof or Offer), batched every Sunday; Stories five days a week; one Live per month before festive seasons.

Paid: about 1,000 naira per day: two-thirds to a cold Reel ad in Jos, one-third to retargeting people who engaged in the last 60 days. Break-even cost per order: 4,000 naira, based on her profit per outfit.
Partners: one micro-influencer in Jos in month 2, and a Collab with a local shoe maker.
Review: last Saturday of each month, using her tracking sheet; write three decisions.
blocks.result: Hauwa knows exactly what to do each week, how much she will spend, and how she will judge success. At day 90 she compares results with her goals and writes the next plan.

items: **Month 1:** set up profiles, catalogue, labels and tracking; post consistently; small test ads.
**Month 2:** do more of the best formats from month 1; add retargeting; one partnership.
**Month 3:** scale ads that are below break-even; plan for the next season or holiday; write the next 90-day plan.

blocks.text: Running your monthly review

Set a fixed date each month for your review, for example the last Saturday, and give it one hour. Open your tracking sheet, Insights and Ads Manager. Answer five questions in writing: Did we reach our goals for the month? Which three posts brought the most enquiries or orders? Which platform or format took time but brought little? What did ads cost per order compared with break-even? What will we do more of, less of, and try new next month?

Turn the answers into three clear decisions, such as "two Proof posts a week instead of one", "pause the Facebook interest ad" and "test one TikTok video a week". Write them at the top of next month's calendar. At the end of 90 days, compare your results with the goals you set at the start, celebrate what improved, and write the next 90-day plan using what you have learned about your own customers. Over a year, four cycles of plan, act, measure and adjust will teach you more about your market than any general advice.

Share your plan with anyone who helps you, such as a family member who packs orders or a friend who films videos, so everyone knows the posting days, the offers coming up and how quickly customers must be answered. A plan that lives only in your head is easy to forget during a busy week; a written one on the wall or in your phone keeps the whole team on track.

blocks.title: Plan around Nigerian seasons
blocks.text: Wedding seasons, Christmas, Eid, Easter, back-to-school and end-of-year office parties change what people buy. Mark them on your calendar and start promoting two to four weeks before.

blocks.title: Protect your time
blocks.text: Only plan what you can keep. Three posts a week for 12 weeks beats daily posting for two weeks and then silence.

takeaways: A strategy is a plan for limited time and money to reach a clear goal
Set SMART goals linked to enquiries and sales
Put platforms, content, community, ads, partners and measurement into one plan
Review monthly and adjust using your tracking sheet
Plan around seasons and only commit to what you can sustain

Fill in each part of the plan table for your business.

Mark key seasons and your three monthly review dates on a calendar.
Share the plan with one person who will ask you about it each month.

quiz.q: A Reel reached 2,000 accounts and got 100 engagements. What is its engagement rate?
quiz.explain: Engagement rate = 100 ÷ 2,000 × 100 = 5 percent.

quiz.q: Zainab's product photo had low reach but brought 11 WhatsApp chats. What does this show?
options: Reach is the only number that matters
A post with smaller reach can still drive more sales actions when it has a price and clear call to action
quiz.explain: Business results like messages and orders matter more than reach alone.

quiz.q: Ifeoma is choosing between a celebrity with 2 million followers across Africa and a food reviewer with 15,000 followers mostly in Owerri. Her bakery only delivers in Owerri. Which is the better first choice?
options: The local food reviewer, after checking engagement and audience Insights
Whoever is cheaper without checking anything
quiz.explain: Audience fit with where you deliver matters most; a smaller local audience can bring more real orders.

quiz.q: A buyer sends an SMS-style credit alert and asks you to ship now. What should you do?
options: Ship, because the alert looks official
Ask the buyer to send the alert again
Refund the buyer to be safe
Confirm the payment in your own bank or payment app first
quiz.explain: Fake alerts are a common scam. Only your own bank or payment app confirms that money has arrived.

quiz.q: Which is a SMART social media goal?
options: Get 60 WhatsApp enquiries and 20 orders from Instagram between January and March
Have the best page in Nigeria
quiz.explain: It is specific, measurable, achievable, relevant to sales and has a time limit.

quiz.q: Hauwa's tracking sheet shows Reels bring followers but Proof posts bring more orders. What should she do in month 2?
options: Keep Reels for reach and add more Proof posts, then measure again
Ignore the sheet and copy a competitor
quiz.explain: The monthly cycle is to measure, decide and adjust, doing more of what drives each goal.

finalQuiz.q: Which statement best describes the role of WhatsApp Business for most Nigerian small businesses on social media?
options: It replaces the need for any other platform
It is mainly for running paid ads
It is where enquiries are answered and sales are closed after people discover you elsewhere
It is only for personal chats
finalQuiz.explain: Facebook, Instagram and TikTok help people discover you; WhatsApp Business is usually where you answer, confirm payment and close the sale.

finalQuiz.q: Which item is MOST important to include in an Instagram bio for a business?
options: How to order, such as a wa.me WhatsApp link
finalQuiz.explain: A visitor must know how to order. A click-to-chat link turns interest into a conversation.

finalQuiz.q: Why do saves and shares matter on Instagram and TikTok?
options: They are only visible to you
They signal that people value the post, which helps it reach more people
finalQuiz.explain: Ranking systems use reactions such as saves and shares as signs a post is worth showing to more people.

finalQuiz.q: What is the recommended size for a Reel or Story?
finalQuiz.explain: Reels and Stories are vertical, full-screen 9:16 content, usually 1080 x 1920 pixels.

finalQuiz.q: A short product video gets many views but few enquiries. Which change is most likely to help?
options: Add a clear call to action with price and how to order
Use music from outside the app
finalQuiz.explain: Views without action usually mean people did not know what to do next. A clear CTA with price and ordering steps fixes that.

finalQuiz.q: What is the best way to handle an honest public complaint?
options: Delete it and block the customer
Ask friends to post positive comments under it
Ignore it until it goes away
Reply calmly in public, then solve it in private chat
finalQuiz.explain: A calm public reply shows other customers you care; the details and fix happen privately.

finalQuiz.q: In Meta Ads Manager, which level holds the campaign objective?
finalQuiz.explain: Each campaign has one objective. Ad sets hold the audience and budget; ads hold the creative.

finalQuiz.q: Which audience is a retargeting audience?
options: Women 25 to 45 in Lagos interested in fashion
People who engaged with your Instagram account in the last 60 days
finalQuiz.explain: Retargeting uses a custom audience of people who have already interacted with your business.

finalQuiz.q: An ad spent 12,000 naira and brought 30 conversations and 6 orders. What is the cost per order?
finalQuiz.explain: Cost per order = 12,000 ÷ 6 = 2,000 naira. Compare it with your profit per order to know if the ad pays.

finalQuiz.q: A post reached 4,000 accounts and got 200 engagements. What is the engagement rate?
Before paying an influencer, what should a small business check first?
options: Whether they have a blue badge
Audience location and age, real comments, and average views
finalQuiz.explain: Audience fit and genuine engagement predict results far better than follower count alone.

finalQuiz.q: Which is the safest way to confirm a customer has paid before shipping?
options: Checking your own bank or payment app
A voice note saying they have paid
finalQuiz.explain: Screenshots and SMS alerts can be faked. Only your own bank or payment app confirms that money has arrived.
